    def _emit_loop_scoped_finally_blocks(self) -> None:
        """Run finally bodies that belong to the current innermost loop.

        For break/continue: only the try/finally frames opened INSIDE the
        innermost loop must run (an outer try/finally wrapping the whole
        loop runs via natural fall-through, not on break/continue). A frame
        opened inside the current loop was pushed when len(self.loop_stack)
        equalled its current value (the loop is still on the stack during
        break/continue emission), so match on that depth.
        """
        stack = self._finally_stack
        if not stack or self._emitting_finally:
            return
        cur_depth = len(self.loop_stack)
        prev = self._emitting_finally
        self._emitting_finally = True
        idx = len(stack) - 1
        while idx >= 0:
            if self._builder_block_is_terminated():
                self._emitting_finally = prev
                return
            body, depth = stack[idx]
            if depth == cur_depth:
                self._emit_stmts(body)
            idx -= 1
        self._emitting_finally = prev
proposed_edits.note: Updates the return-path reader to unpack the new (body, depth) tuple (return runs ALL frames regardless of depth -- correct, it exits the whole function), and adds the loop-scoped variant for break/continue.
Run loop-scoped finally before branching. Guard with _builder_block_is_terminated() in case the finally body itself returns/raises/breaks.

confirmed_gaps.observed: AttributeError: __cause__ when reading e.__cause__ on a USER exception subclass instance. (And the `from e` cause is silently dropped: py_exc_set_cause is a no-op for non-PY_TYPE_EXC objects.)
confirmed_gaps.expected: e.__cause__ is the KeyError (CPython prints 'cause type KeyError'); __context__ likewise.
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: User exception subclasses are PyInstanceObject (PY_TYPE_INSTANCE), not the builtin PyExceptionObject (PY_TYPE_EXC). (1) pcc/runtime/src/py_exc_objects.c py_exc_set_cause/py_exc_set_context early-return unless py_type_of(exc)==PY_TYPE_EXC, so `raise UserExc(...) from e` stores nothing on the user instance. (2) py_obj_ops_dispatch.c instance getattr has no __cause__/__context__ defaulting, so reading e.__cause__ on a user instance hits missing-attr -> AttributeError instead of the CPython default None. Bounded fix: make py_exc_set_cause/py_exc_set_context store onto a PY_TYPE_INSTANCE via py_obj_setattr(exc, "__cause__"/"__context__", v); and make instance getattr return py_None for __cause__/__context__ when unset. This is a both-tier runtime change (py_exc_objects.c + py_exc_objects.py, plus py_obj_ops_dispatch instance getattr both tiers) and interacts with GC slot storage, so validate against the bootstrap gate.

proposed_edits.note: LOW CONFIDENCE: storing __cause__ as an instance attr works for read-back via instance getattr, but reading an UNSET __cause__ on a user instance still needs a None default (separate edit in instance getattr) to fully match CPython. Verify py_obj_setattr is declared in this TU and handles PY_TYPE_INSTANCE.

LOW CONFIDENCE: mirror of set_cause for context. Same caveats; the port py_exc_objects.py must be mirrored. The None-default-on-read for unset __context__ on user instances is a further separate change in instance getattr (both tiers).

confirmed_gaps.observed: pcc prints 'context None' (implicit __context__ is not set when a new exception is raised inside an except handler)
confirmed_gaps.expected: CPython prints 'context first' (the in-flight ValueError becomes __context__ of the RuntimeError)
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: The runtime py_raise() (pcc/runtime/src/py_exc_tls.c ~line 133) auto-chains __context__ from the still-pending TLS exception. But the frontend (pcc/frontends/python/codegen/exception_lowering.py _emit_try) calls py_clear_exception() at handler ENTRY (line 532) BEFORE running the handler body, so by the time `raise RuntimeError(...)` runs the TLS slot is already clear and py_raise sees cur==NULL. Worse, for a handler with no `as` name and no bare re-raise, retain_handler_exc is False (line 529), so the handler exception is not even kept in _active_handler_excs. Bounded frontend fix: when a handler body may raise, keep handler_exc retained and, in _emit_raise for an explicit exc with no `from`, set __context__ to _active_handler_excs[-1] via py_exc_set_context. This touches the bootstrap-critical handler retain/release lifecycle, so validate against the bootstrap gate.

proposed_edits.old_string: retain_handler_exc = h.name is not None or body_has_bare_raise(h.body)
proposed_edits.new_string:
retain_handler_exc = (
                h.name is not None
                or body_has_bare_raise(h.body)
                or body_has_any_raise(h.body)
            )
proposed_edits.note: LOW CONFIDENCE. Keep the handler exception alive whenever the handler body contains any raise, so a new exception raised in the handler can chain its __context__ to it. Requires adding a body_has_any_raise() helper (analogous to body_has_bare_raise but matching Raise nodes with exc != None too) and, in _emit_raise's explicit-exc branch, when getattr(self,'_active_handler_excs',()) is non-empty and stmt.cause is None, call self.builder.call(self.runtime['py_exc_set_context'], [exc_val, active_stack[-1]]) before py_raise. Needs careful GC validation; the runtime already guards existing_context==NULL but the frontend call would set unconditionally on a freshly-built exc (safe since its context starts NULL).

confirmed_gaps.observed: pcc str(e) -> 'a' and repr(e) -> ValueError('a'); only the FIRST constructor argument is retained.
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: Exception construction is single-arg-only end to end: pcc/frontends/python/codegen/exception_lowering.py _build_exception_value()/_message_cstr() pass only args[0] to py_exc_new(tag, cstr); PyExceptionObject has a single `message` PyObject field (pcc/runtime/src/py_internal.h ~line 770) and no args tuple; py_obj_str / repr for PY_TYPE_EXC format only `message`. Faithfully fixing multi-arg requires (a) capturing the full args tuple at construction (new runtime entrypoint e.g. py_exc_new_with_args(cls, args_tuple) and frontend lowering of all positional args), (b) storing an args field on PyExceptionObject, and (c) str/repr formatting per CPython BaseException rules (0 args -> '', 1 arg -> str(arg), >1 -> str(tuple)). This is a larger multi-file change; flagged for backlog, not a one-line patch.
